title: I Checked What $10,000 in My 10 Favorite Stocks Would Be Worth Today
creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; Oracle's exact year-to-date percentage was garbled in the captions and is not stated.
summary: Couch Investor works out what $10,000 invested on 1 January 2026 in each of his 10 favourite stocks would be worth now, using Fiscal.ai data, on a half-day Friday after Thanksgiving. Among semiconductors, Micron is still up 110% year to date, AMD 89%, Marvell 54%, Intel 47.6%, ASML 21.8%, Applied Materials 21.1%, TSMC 12.7%, KLA 10.4% and Lam Research 8.1%, while Qualcomm, Broadcom and Nvidia are red year to date. In big tech, Apple is the outperformer at up 30.8%, Amazon is up 5.9% and Microsoft barely up 1.3%; Meta and Alphabet are down slightly, Tesla is down 15.5%, Netflix is down 36.6% and Oracle is down (exact figure garbled in captions). Across the VanEck Semiconductor ETF names, valuations look cheap versus history, and the median forward PE of the big-tech and internet group is 23.4x, with Oracle at about 12.6x and Reddit at 13.1x - though he stresses a low PE alone is not a buy, since slow growth, high capex, debt and macro all explain the discounts. In software and fintech (Palantir, Shopify, Netflix, Uber, Axon, FICO, Robinhood, SoFi), most names are also much cheaper than their 10-year medians, and 7 of 16 names are down more than half from their 52-week highs, FICO 62%. He calls SoFi 'a bargain in my opinion' (22.6x trailing, about 14.2-14.5x forward earnings, revenue up 42% year on year, with 2027 guidance already given). No explicit buy or sell calls are made in the video.
